confidence_reason: Water extents are a terrain-model reconstruction with illustrative stages; only the late-recession size is checked against radar, and spatial agreement there is weak.

area.en: Mae Sai District, Chiang Rai, Thailand (the image footprint also covers Tachileik, Myanmar)
area.th: อำเภอแม่สาย จังหวัดเชียงราย (ภาพครอบคลุมท่าขี้เหล็ก เมียนมาด้วย)

depth_factor.reference: Sai River main stem at the Mae Sai border bridges

model_coverage.reason: The Copernicus DEM tile used stops at 100°E; district land east of it is not modelled.

summary.en: Normal conditions in Mae Sai. Northern Thailand had seen heavy rain since mid-August, but the Sai River stayed within safe levels.
summary.th: สภาพในแม่สายยังปกติ ภาคเหนือมีฝนตกหนักต่อเนื่องตั้งแต่กลางเดือนสิงหาคม แต่แม่น้ำสายยังอยู่ในระดับปลอดภัย

summary.en: Torrential rain from the remnants of Typhoon Yagi. The Sai River rose fast and overflowed into homes and the border market during the night.
summary.th: ฝนตกหนักมากจากอิทธิพลที่เหลือของพายุไต้ฝุ่นยางิ แม่น้ำสายเพิ่มระดับอย่างรวดเร็วและล้นเข้าบ้านเรือนและตลาดชายแดนในช่วงกลางคืน

label.th: ระดับสูงสุด

summary.en: The worst flash flooding. Very swift, deep water submerged ground floors; power was cut, hundreds of residents were stranded on rooftops and rescue boats struggled against the current.
summary.th: ช่วงน้ำท่วมฉับพลันรุนแรงที่สุด กระแสน้ำเชี่ยวและลึกจนท่วมชั้นล่างของอาคาร ไฟฟ้าถูกตัด ประชาชนหลายร้อยคนติดอยู่บนหลังคา และเรือกู้ภัยฝ่ากระแสน้ำได้ยาก

summary.en: Rain eased and the Sai River fell gradually. Main roads reopened to heavy vehicles while low-lying plains stayed under water.
summary.th: ฝนเริ่มซาและระดับแม่น้ำสายค่อย ๆ ลดลง ถนนสายหลักเริ่มให้รถขนาดใหญ่สัญจรได้ แต่พื้นที่ราบลุ่มต่ำยังมีน้ำท่วมขัง

label.th: น้ำลดเกือบหมด

summary.en: UNOSAT monitoring reported that most remaining surface water had disappeared or shrunk sharply by 19 September.
summary.th: การติดตามของ UNOSAT รายงานว่าน้ำผิวดินที่เหลือส่วนใหญ่หายไปหรือลดลงอย่างมากภายในวันที่ 19 กันยายน

reported.name_en: Mae Sai Subdistrict Municipality Office shelter and relief centre
reported.name_th: ศูนย์พักพิงเทศบาลตำบลแม่สาย (สำนักงานเทศบาลตำบลแม่สาย)
reported.tambon: เวียงพางคำ (the OSM address puts the office in Ban Pa Yang Mai, Wiang Phang Kham; the municipality covers parts of ต.แม่สาย and ต.เวียงพางคำ)
reported.location_evidence: OSM way 371846370 'สำนักงานเทศบาลตำบลแม่สาย' / 'Maesai Municipality Office' (amenity=townhall), https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/371846370 ; coordinates are the Nominatim centroid, and the Overpass center 20.4265324, 99.8843686 agrees
reported.period_used: Open by the early hours of 2024-09-11 (34 people at 01:00). Occupancy 53 on the ICC report covering 9-15 Sep (published 2024-09-16), 49 on 2024-09-21 and 41 on 2024-09-28. Still open at 87 on 2024-10-08/10 after the early-October re-flood. The municipal relief/command centre was set up in the same building on 2024-09-11.

sources.title: รวมเบอร์ติดต่อ "ขอความช่วยเหลือ-แจ้งเหตุ" น้ำท่วม จ.เชียงราย
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: As of 01:00 on 11 Sep 2024, 34 evacuees were at the Mae Sai municipality shelter and 37 at Wat Phrom Wihan. It lists the Mae Sai flood shelters as เทศบาลตำบลแม่สาย and วัดพรหมวิหาร.

sources.title: เปิดพิกัด 'ศูนย์พักพิง-จุดจอดรถ' ช่วยเหลือ น้ำท่วมเชียงราย
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Under the heading for Mae Sai flood shelters, it lists two sites: เทศบาลตำบลแม่สาย and วัดพรหมวิหาร.

sources.title: เทศบาลแม่สายได้จัดตั้งศูนย์อำนวยการช่วยเหลือผู้ประสบภัยน้ำท่วม
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: The municipality set up a flood relief command centre in the Mae Sai municipal office building, reachable on hotline 199.

sources.title: UPDATE สถานการณ์น้ำท่วม และการช่วยเหลือผู้ประสบภัย 13 กันยายน 2567
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: DDPM daily update: in Mae Sai, a local-government shelter was set up at เทศบาลตำบลแม่สาย.

sources.title: ศูนย์บัญชาการเหตุการณ์ฯ สรุปสถานการณ์อุทกภัย เชียงราย กระทบ 9 อำเภอ 53,209 ครัวเรือน เสียชีวิต 12 ราย
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Chiang Rai ICC report for 9-15 Sep: 17 shelters open in Mae Sai holding 1,343 people. This site had 53 people and a medical team.

sources.title: น้ำท่วมเชียงราย กระทบพื้นที่เกษตรไปแล้ว 14,138 ไร่ และ โรงเรียนอีก 31 แห่ง
sources.publisher: nakornchiangrainews (credits Chiang Rai Provincial PR Office)
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: As of 21 Sep: 6 Mae Sai shelters with 501 people. This site had 49 remaining.

sources.title: ข้อมูลน้ำท่วมเชียงราย 9-28 ก.ย.67 เสียชีวิต 13 เจ็บ 3 สูญหาย 1 ราย
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: As of 28 Sep: 3 Mae Sai shelters with 237 people. This site had 41 remaining.

sources.title: ศูนย์บัญชาการเหตุการณ์ฯ รายงานสถานการณ์อุทกภัย และดินถล่ม ในพื้นที่จังหวัดเชียงราย ประจำวันที่ 10 ตุลาคม 2567
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Mae Sai still had 3 shelters open, with 87 people remaining at the municipality shelter.

reported.notes: This was the primary municipal shelter from the first night of the Sep 2024 flood through October. Take capacity figures from the 2025 events (the July 2025 Khaosod list gives about 200) only as indicative. The same building was the municipal relief/command centre.
reported.reported_capacity_or_occupancy: Occupancy: 34 (2024-09-11 01:00), 53 (about 2024-09-15), 49 (2024-09-21), 41 (2024-09-28), 87 (2024-10-10). Capacity was not reported for Sep 2024. A July 2025 municipal list gives about 200, which comes from a different event.
reported.access_set_note: Reported in use by 15 Sep (ICC 9-15 Sep list or earlier reports); exact opening time not modelled.

reported.name_th: ศูนย์พักพิงชั่วคราว วัดพรหมวิหาร
reported.tambon: เวียงพางคำ
reported.location_evidence: OSM way 372716639 'วัดพรหมวิหาร' / 'Wat Prom Wihan' (amenity=place_of_worship, buddhist), https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/372716639 ; coordinates are the Nominatim centroid, and the Overpass center 20.4264275, 99.8799585 agrees. Tambon ต.เวียงพางคำ is confirmed by PRD.
reported.period_used: Open by 2024-09-11 01:00 (37 people). The Thammanat Foundation set up a relief centre and kitchen here and trucked evacuees in on 2024-09-12. The PM visited the shelter on 2024-09-13. Occupancy 341 about 2024-09-15 and 119 on 2024-09-21. It is not in the 2024-09-28 list, so it closed between 21 and 28 Sep. It was used as an aid-distribution venue on 2024-09-28.

sources.title: นายกฯ สวมกอดให้กำลังใจผู้ประสบภัย อ.แม่สาย ...

sources.quote_or_paraphrase: On 12 Sep a foundation set up a relief centre and temporary kitchen at Wat Phrom Wihan and used six-wheel trucks to move trapped residents to the shelter there.

sources.quote_or_paraphrase: ICC 9-15 Sep list: the Wat Phrom Wihan shelter held 341 people, with medical teams from Mae Sai Hospital, MCATT and others.

sources.quote_or_paraphrase: The PM travelled to Phrom Wihan Temple in Mae Sai and distributed compensation to flood-hit families.

reported.notes: This was a core shelter from the first night. The Mae Sai Municipal School 1 (โรงเรียนเทศบาล 1 วัดพรหมวิหาร) sits in the temple grounds. A May 2025 Thai PBS World item lists 'Municipal School 1' as a separate shelter, but that is a different event. I found no Sep 2024 source that names the school separately.

sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Most residents of the mud-buried Tham Pha Chom community were staying in shelters, especially at nearby Wat Tham Pha Chom, where agencies delivered food daily.

sources.title: Deadly Thai floods intensified by climate change, La Niña displace 150,000 families
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: A monk says about 300 people came to stay at the temple after the flood and about 150 were still living there.

sources.title: ช่อง 3 เดินหน้าส่งกำลังใจพี่น้องชาวแม่สาย ลงพื้นที่ร่วมให้ความช่วยเหลือผู้ประสบอุทกภัย

reported.notes: The temple is next to the worst-hit riverside zone (Hua Fai / Tham Pha Chom). The community there was buried under 2-3 m of mud, but I found no report that the temple itself was flooded. The Rajabhat relief team's community kitchen was also at this temple in July 2025, which is a different event.

sources.quote_or_paraphrase: The Wat Mueang Daeng shelter was still open on 10 Oct with 50-52 people.

reported.notes: The temple sits inside the heavily flooded Mueang Daeng community (flood zone 3 in the ICC's 5-zone plan). Its own monks were evacuated at the peak. It became a shelter after the water receded, probably for residents whose homes were mud-filled. Replay logic should not treat it as usable on 11-13 Sep.
reported.access_set_note: The temple was itself flooded and evacuated at the peak; it served as a shelter from 21 Sep.

sources.quote_or_paraphrase: As of 21 Sep, 17 people remained at the MSDHS-run Baan Ua-Arthorn Mae Sai 1 shelter.

reported.notes: This was a shelter for vulnerable groups (elderly, disabled, children). The location is weak, so geocode it properly before use.
reported.reported_capacity_or_occupancy: Capacity 50 (MSDHS, 2024-09-14). Occupancy 17 (2024-09-21). MSDHS also prepared 'แม่สาย 2' (capacity 50), but I found no occupancy reported for it.
reported.access_set_note: Prepared as a shelter for vulnerable groups by 14 Sep, after the peak.

shelters.confidence_reason: Candidates are OSM public buildings with sparse footprints; eligibility and coverage use the reconstructed peak and walking distance, not site surveys.
shelters.source_timestamp: OSM extract 2026-07-09; reported shelters compiled 2026-09-27 from reports dated 2024-09-11 to 2024-10-11
shelters.reported_status: Reported use from public sources; not an official register. Locations are OSM matches where possible; low-confidence locations are approximate.
shelters.reported_access_set_rule: The reported_2024 access set counts located sites reported as overnight shelters by 15 Sep; the command centre and sites first used after 12 Sep are shown on the map but not counted. Opening times within 10-12 Sep are not modelled.

Event chronology (phases and narrative)
sources.attribution: FloodGuard team summary of public reporting; not independently verified in this study

assumptions: Daily water surfaces are a HAND (height above nearest drainage) threshold reconstruction, not observations.

Stage keyframes (metres above the mapped channel) are illustrative values shaped to the event chronology; no gauge record was used. The stage is held at 0 through 9 Sep and rises through the night of 10 Sep.
The stage is the assumed Sai main-stem level at the Mae Sai bridges; tributaries rise k x stage (see the next assumption). Real water levels still differed reach by reach.
Drainage channels are cells with at least 25 km² of upstream area on the 30 m Copernicus DSM; buildings and trees in the DSM bias HAND upward in town.

Roads are impassable when reconstructed depth reaches 0.3 m at any 10 m sample along a 120 m piece (per-sample depth factor; the exported k makes h + 0.3/k equal the earliest sample closure); river-channel samples on bridges are ignored.
Road pieces whose lowest HAND exceeds 4 m never flood under these keyframes and are omitted, except trunk, primary and secondary roads.
The 16 September 06:16 ICT Sentinel-1 pass constrains the size of the late-recession extent only; the two radar passes use different orbit directions.
The onset is shaped by GISTDA's RADARSAT-2 figure for 10 Sep 18:15 (about 9.9 km2 flooded in Mae Sai) and reports of an overnight surge; the 11 Sep 02:00 knot (2.5 m) is illustrative.
Cells that drain off the DEM tile (east of 100°E, towards the Ruak) before meeting a mapped channel use their outlet on the tile edge as the HAND reference.
Where flow routing leaves no path to a channel (large flats), HAND falls back to height above the nearest channel cell.

Stage varies along the river: each cell's water rise is scaled by k = clip((A / A_Sai) ** 0.3, 0.35, 1), where A is the upstream area of its drainage channel and A_Sai the Sai main stem at the Mae Sai bridges (downstream hydraulic geometry). Cells draining east off the tile are treated as main-river (k = 1).
People in water uses WorldPop 2020 (100 m, spread evenly over 10 m cells); it is modelled residential population, not the 2024 population or tourists and traders at the border market.

Evacuation access uses the repo road graph and walking distance: a resident node has access when an open, dry shelter is within 2 km along roads still passable (about 30 minutes on foot); a road closes at 0.3 m of reconstructed depth and a shelter stops serving once water reaches it. Levels are evaluated every 0.05 m of stage.

Shelter candidates are OpenStreetMap public buildings and grounds (schools, places of worship, government offices, community centres; OSM amenity=shelter huts are excluded). A candidate is eligible only if it keeps 0.5 m freeboard at the modelled peak and a road node lies within 400 m. Ranking is greedy maximal coverage of residents whose homes are wet at the peak, within 2 km walking on normal roads (pre-emptive evacuation); late_cumulative_share repeats the check on roads still open at 1.0 m stage.

Shelter capacity = mapped OSM building footprint within the site x 0.5 usable share / 3.5 m² per person (Sphere minimum covered space); OSM building coverage in Mae Sai is sparse, so many capacities are unknown or underestimated.
Flash-flood velocity, debris and mud deposition are not modelled.
limitations: Not a real-time product or an official warning; for preparedness learning and post-event prioritisation only.
No satellite image exists for 10-14 September over Mae Sai in these inputs; onset and peak extents are not observed.
Statistics cover only the modelled parts of the eight Mae Sai subdistricts (see model_coverage); roads and facilities outside the model are flagged m=false and excluded.
